items.summary: tmux status-interval 1 had six #() programs for statusbar, on battery that was 15.4% of a core. After digging found fork+exec through sh -c is ~14.6 ms and computing the actual segments was 2.6 ms on my device. Plus had ~1.5k lines of zsh scripts. Now one deamon process, caches in memory, unix socket and one #() for the whole right side. From 153.77 ms/s → 18.43 ms/s. Made that into a tmux plugin. items.title: Show HN: Palette, a Figma plugin that turns one color into a whole UI system
items.summary: I was inspired to build this because of AI slop design. That led me down the path of why computers didn't 'see' color the way that humans did - and the lack of a common language between perceptual, display, and print color spaces (there was no Unicode for color). That led me to inventing and patenting ART, a new color language, and Orchestra, the engine that runs it. Palette is the first product built on this tech, and it solves problems I faced as a designer for the last 30 years: - Colors that shift when you make them lighter or darker - The RGB color wheel tells you colors should look good

Show HN: Warble – Share voice notes in your social media feeds
items.summary: Hey HN, I built Warble because I noticed that you can't currently share voice notes to your main social feeds. With Warble you can simply record a voice note, choose a theme, and warble quickly renders out a video you can share. No editing required, no need to get on camera. The output isn't genAI video, the videos themselves are pre-designed motion templates (I'm primarily a motion designer). AI is used in a small way to transcribe the voice note and provide the captions which are then animated within each of the themes. I've been using it myself to post over on LinkedIn for a month or so now
